Integration branch for the imbue_cloud slice-fleet generation 2 program (raw qemu slices with routed-tap networking on Debian 13 boxes, replacing lima), merged together with `main` and the three pre-cutover fix PRs: imbue-ai/mngr-internal#857 (SSH certificates from Vault, #850), #855 (DHCP placement, #849) and #856 (the upstream artifact mirror, #851). The per-change details live in this directory's constituent entries, listed below.

The gen-2 operator tooling: box ordering/prep/setup for generation 2 (WireGuard management overlay, `:22` lockdown, box telemetry, DHCP server, CA-trust-only management SSH, mirror-sourced downloads), the `cutover` command group, `wireguard` and `artifacts` commands, and the per-tier operator identity directory `~/.mindsadmin/<tier>/`.

Constituent entries: `new-fleet-base.md`, `new-fleet-runsc-prototype.md`, `new-fleet-phase-2.md`, `new-fleet-phase-3.md`, `new-fleet-phase-4-impl.md`, `new-fleet-phase-5.5.md`, `mngr-variable-sizing.md`, `mngr-slice-fleet-gen2-phase-2.md`, `mngr-slice-fleet-gen2-phase-3.md`, `mngr-slice-fleet-gen2-phase-4.md`, `mngr-new-fleet-testing.md`, `mngr-slice-fleet-canary-followups.md`, `mngr-finish-new-fleet-canary-testing.md`, `mngr-identify-new-fleet-issues.md`, `mngr-design-network-observation.md`, `mngr-onetun-install-and-canary.md`, `mngr-lima-rename.md`, `mngr-ssh-authority-in-vault.md`, `mngr-remove-init-via-dhcp.md`, `mngr-mirror-upstream-artifacts.md`

Gen-2 small follow-ups: `minds-admin` reads a tier's gen-2 management plane from the `[management_plane]` table of its `deploy.toml` instead of the deleted `management_plane.toml` (env deploy's proxy attach, the gen-2 prep's WireGuard peers and `:22` allowlist, the userspace-tunnel dial, and the `wireguard` commands, whose refusal messages now point at the table).

`minds-admin artifacts verify` now also probes each stored artifact's public mirror URL and reports `UNSERVED` (exit 1) when the bucket holds it but the live Worker does not serve it -- the Worker's route table deploys separately from the bucket's content, and the bucket-only check passed on 2026-09-09 while every artifact URL answered 400.

Gen-2 small follow-ups: `minds-admin server register` no longer refuses a delivered gen-2 box whose disk holds fewer than its RAM's full complement of default machines; it registers with a warning stating how many fit (the prep re-measures `disk_gb`, and the two-budget accounting fits fewer machines). `server order` keeps refusing such configs. The box-management dial now warns, rather than logging at debug, when the tier lists WireGuard operators but no operator key is at `~/.mindsadmin/<tier>/wireguard.key`, since a locked-down box is then unreachable with no visible reason.

`minds-admin env destroy` now refuses, before any remote teardown, while local processes still hold the env root -- a minds desktop backend launched with the env's `client.toml`, or a `mngr latchkey forward` supervisor owning the env's latchkey directory (detected through its lock) -- naming each with a stop hint; `--stop-local-processes` SIGTERMs them (desktop first, then the supervisor, whose teardown stops the gateway, `mngr observe`, and the tunnels) and waits for them to exit. Previously the destroy removed every remote resource under a still-running desktop and then failed at the very end because the mngr host dir was being written to while the env root was deleted.

`test_deployments.py services-against` now records the target env's pool in the run config -- the largest group of available rows sharing one template repo, ref, and region, read from the env's DB (`--pool-region` picks the region when several have rows) -- so the pool-backed tests (the fast-path create above all) run against an operator's dev env instead of skipping for lack of pool info.

`minds-admin cutover rollback` now re-stamps the row's recorded VM and container SSH host keys with the keys the migrate harvested when it rolls back a mid-migration failure. The product restore brings the gen-1 VM back with the keys it had at the stop but at fresh ports, and clients pin the row's recorded values for any endpoint they hold no pin of their own for -- so a row still carrying the bake-time keys of a client-rotated (adopted) VM left every client unable to SSH to the rolled-back workspace ("Host key ... does not match") until the pins were repaired by hand. A rollback of a completed migration is unaffected (the finish CAS already stamped the harvested keys).

`minds-admin pool destroy` now says why it refuses a young `baking` row (its bake may still be running; retry once it is older than the orphan age guard) instead of the contradictory "unexpected status 'baking' (claimable: ... baking ...)".

A slice bake killed by SIGTERM/SIGINT mid-create now re-opens its box dial before the orphan reap (the recursive worker kill also took the WireGuard tunnel down, so the reap used to be skipped with "Connection refused") and deletes the `baking` rows of the killed workers instead of leaving them for the two-hour age guard.

`minds-admin cutover migrate` / `rollback` / `repave` now let Ctrl-C end the process immediately (the default SIGINT action, as SIGTERM already did) instead of a KeyboardInterrupt that could leave a migrate polling for minutes; the stages resume from their state files on the next run.

`minds-admin server import-boxes` skips (and reports under `skipped`) a source box the target DB already registers under another row id -- the `ovh_service_name` unique index used to abort the whole import.

`minds-admin repair-home-layout` (new on main) is gen-1 only on this branch: a leased slice whose box is gen-2 is skipped with a warning and counted as unreachable, because the repair runs its in-VM script through the lima client's `run_in_vm_as_root` (`limactl shell`), which a raw-qemu slice has no counterpart for. Its box dial and service user now resolve the same way as every other box command (`resolve_server_management_dial` / `box_service_user`).


Fixed (found while repaving the dev boxes for storage encryption, 2026-09-11): `cutover repave` of a drained gen-2 box failed with "server ... is draining; run `await-delivery` until it is `delivered` first". The repave only moved gen-1 boxes to `delivered` before handing off to the reinstall, so the drain-then-repave path the storage-encryption runbook prescribes for a box prepped before encryption existed never reached the reinstall. A drained gen-2 box is now flipped to `delivered` too (`repave_pre_reinstall_server_fields`); a gen-2 box already `delivered` or `installing` still resumes as before. The repave's `--dry-run` outcome now names the columns that run would set for the box (it used to describe the gen-1 flip for every box).


Fixed (found repaving the dev boxes, 2026-09-11): a gen-2 `server setup` / `cutover repave` failed after its prep script had completed, with "ssh: connect to host <box> port 22: Connection refused". The prep script installs the box's `:22` lockdown, but the storage-encryption round trips that follow it (the LUKS header-backup fetch and the passphrase-staging cleanup) kept dialing the public address the fresh reinstall had answered on, and the refused connection surfaced wrapped in a concurrency-group exception the best-effort handlers did not catch, so the row stayed `installing` with its new WireGuard key unrecorded. Now the prep (under `server setup` and `server prep` alike) records the box's WireGuard key as soon as the script returns and runs the follow-up round trips through the management resolver (the overlay tunnel, or the public address for a box with no overlay yet); a resume from `installing` dials the resolver too; and the SSH script runner hands the wrapped `BareMetalProvisioningError` back to every caller (the prep's storage round trips, `wireguard sync-peers`, and the cutover disk transplant catch the plain error).
